clue.text: Impossible to scoff about British excelling all others

indicators.note: the phrase for not edible wraps itself around the abbreviation, standing on either side of it

blocks.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so impossible to scoff is inedible
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A dish so delicious nobody could resist it, or a British champion beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff is British slang for wolfing food down, and the phrase is not built from a word for impossible: the whole expression means inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody can defeat in competition outdoes every rival, so it surpasses the whole field.

clue.text: Ill-equipped group of soldiers — 20 in it

indicators.note: in it places the cross-referenced letter inside the military group

blocks.note: a military unit
the answer to 20 across means loudly, abbreviated in music to F

explanation.surface: An army squad of twenty men lacking proper kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is not a number of soldiers but a cross-reference to 20 across, whose meaning is loud, F in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means unsuitable or not properly prepared for a task.

clue.text: Fish for Robeson, say

blocks.note: first meaning: an American freshwater game fish
second meaning: Paul Robeson was an African American singer with a deep low voice

explanation.surface: Choosing which fish to serve the singer Paul Robeson.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Robeson, the American singer and actor famous for Ol' Man River, was a black man with the lowest male voice type.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a North American sporting fish and also describes a Black singer of the lowest vocal register.

clue.text: Staff ladies worked out with aid to become this?

definitions.text: Staff ladies worked out with aid to become this?

indicators.note: worked out means rearranged or exercised, so the letters are put through a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Female employees exercising with a fitness aid in hopes of getting in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: women who work out at the gym hope to end up in fine condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in excellent health, which is what a workout aims to achieve.

clue.text: Controller of bank changed one lira!

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the phrase are given a different order

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bank official exchanging a single Italian lira coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank is not a money bank but an aircraft tilting as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailerons are hinged flaps on a plane's wings that make the aircraft roll or tilt into a turn.

clue.text: Put up with problem of one-off payment

blocks.note: to lump it is to tolerate something
an arithmetic problem is a sum

explanation.surface: Having to tolerate a difficulty over a single settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A single, complete amount paid at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Loudly arguing in cabinet, initially? How unlike ministers!

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: heads of Loudly, arguing, in and cabinet

explanation.surface: Ministers bickering noisily in a cabinet meeting, which seems most unministerial.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ministers are government ones; the definition means ministers of religion, clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means of the laity rather than the clergy, so it describes someone who is not a church minister.

clue.text: A state in the East upset one in India

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down entry turns the word over

blocks.note: taken as written
Mass is short for Massachusetts, a state on the eastern seaboard of the USA

explanation.surface: An eastern state in turmoil, one of those that make up India.
explanation.walkthrough: The state in the East is American, not Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is one of the states of north-eastern India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: The Lady of the Lake?

blocks.note: surface reading: the mysterious enchantress of Arthurian legend, or the Walter Scott poem
setter's reading: a woman's first name which is also the name of a large lake in central Europe

explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance lies between Germany, Switzerland and Austria; the question mark admits that the woman's name is borrowed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name identical to the English name of the Bodensee, so a lady sharing the lake's title.

clue.text: Statistic quoted in talk as a rhetorical device

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: a number mentioned when speaking
second meaning: a metaphor, simile or similar expression

explanation.surface: A speaker citing a number purely for effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any expression used non-literally for effect, such as metaphor or hyperbole.

clue.text: Apprehensive female getting rebuke

blocks.note: F is the usual abbreviation for female
an earful is a sharp telling-off

explanation.surface: A woman nervous because she is about to be told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone anxious or afraid about what may happen next.

clue.text: China's awful nemesis

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the following word's letters are spoiled into another order

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The country China confronting a dreadful arch-enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country, but it is porcelain; MEISSEN is the German town famous for fine porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen porcelain is a celebrated German chinaware, so the name stands for china itself.

clue.text: Do some job-sharing, with appropriate changes

definitions.text: Do some job-sharing, with appropriate changes

blocks.note: surface reading: splitting one post between two part-time workers
setter's reading: people swap over at intervals, each doing the task in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: The changes are changeovers between people, not alterations to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in rotation, one after another, is how a shared task gets passed back and forth.

clue.text: Not satisfied with some gunmetal

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following word is used, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the second to the sixth of this word, dropping g at the front and al at the end

explanation.surface: Someone displeased with a piece of grey bronze alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands or needs that are not met have not been fulfilled, the sense of satisfied here.

clue.text: Drug one may be told to keep off

definitions.text: one may be told to keep off

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for cannabis

blocks.clueFragment: one may be told to keep off
blocks.note: second meaning: the lawn, as in the park sign Keep off the

explanation.surface: A narcotic that users are warned to stay away from.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep off reads as abstain from a drug, but it is the notice on a park lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: It is street slang for marijuana and also the turf that signs forbid walking on.

clue.text: Changing examination

blocks.note: first meaning: switching sides or converting
second meaning: a thorough inspection

explanation.surface: A test that keeps shifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means switching allegiance; hyphenated as a noun it means a careful inspection.

clue.text: Where cabinet-maker does home work

blocks.note: surface reading: a joiner building furniture; setter's reading: the Prime Minister, who picks the Cabinet
setter's reading: the residence on Downing Street is both the PM's home and office

explanation.walkthrough: The Prime Minister lives and works at 10 Downing Street in London, known simply by its house figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Downing Street address is the British premier's official residence and workplace combined.

clue.text: Create havoc to start rebellion, seizing king and queen

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the phrase for starting a revolt takes the royals inside it

blocks.note: to rise up is to rebel
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries spread chaos by capturing the monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The royals go in after the first letter, T(ERR)ORISE, with the queen ahead of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrorise is to fill with fear and spread disorder, a close match for wreaking havoc.

clue.text: To the extent that artists get seated at the front?

indicators.note: at the front says the seating phrase is placed before the other part, leading the answer

blocks.note: sitting on a couch, in a sofa
RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAS

explanation.surface: Front-row seating arranged for painters at some event.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch of seated as being in a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction limits a statement to the degree to which something holds true.

clue.text: Native of former European state lacking power of another

definitions.note: reads with the clue's opening word Native: a native of another country

indicators.note: lacking says something is missing, so a letter is dropped from the old state's name

blocks.note: Prussia was a German kingdom, dissolved in 1947
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone from a vanished European nation who has no strength left.
explanation.walkthrough: Native does double duty: it starts the wordplay and, joined to 'of another', completes the definition, a native of another state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Russia is a native of a different European country from the one in the wordplay.

clue.text: Island's scholar absorbed in Sanskrit work

indicators.note: absorbed in means soaked up inside, so the scholar sits within the text

blocks.note: a sutra is a Sanskrit text of aphorisms
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: An islander academic engrossed in an ancient Indian text.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island west of Java and Borneo.

clue.text: Hear a couple of scores played loudly

indicators.note: Hear tells us to listen to how the number phrase is pronounced, not how it is written

blocks.note: a score is twenty, so two of them make forty

explanation.surface: Listening to two pieces of music performed at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Scores look musical, but they are twenties.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is the musical direction for strong, loud performance, as in the abbreviation f on a score.

clue.text: Frozen jelly I had

blocks.note: a gel is a jelly-like substance
contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls eating a cold, set jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary word for icy cold, from the Latin for frost.

clue.text: About four or six, bowler perhaps gets very angry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hat goes around the number

blocks.note: a bowler is a hat, and lid is slang for a hat
IV is four in Roman numerals, and also six, VI, read the other way

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler furious at being hit for boundaries of four or six runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is a hat, not a cricketer: in cricket, a four or six is a boundary hit off the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is a strong informal word for furious.

clue.text: Pose he contrived with arm to signal thus?

definitions.text: Pose he contrived with arm to signal thus?

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are put into a made-up order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man strikes an arm posture to send a message.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: flag signallers hold their arms in set positions to spell letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag alphabet is sent by holding the arms at particular angles, each position a letter.

clue.text: Power of two men in boat

blocks.note: first meaning: two cubed
second meaning: a rowing crew of that many oarsmen

explanation.surface: The strength of a pair of sailors in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Power reads as strength, but it is the mathematical sense, two raised to a power.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times two times two gives this number, which is also the name of a rowing crew.

clue.text: He scored every season with great skill

definitions.text: He scored every season with great skill

blocks.note: surface reading: a footballer or cricketer scoring goals or runs year after year; setter's reading: a composer who wrote music for all four seasons
the composer's concertos are admired for their virtuosity

explanation.walkthrough: Scored means wrote music, and every season points to The Four Seasons, the Venetian composer's famous violin concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baroque Italian composer wrote a famous set of concertos, one for spring, summer, autumn and winter.

clue.text: Pouring tea, say, with china

indicators.note: say asks us to pronounce the drink's name and spell another word with that sound

blocks.note: a golf peg sounds just like the drink
Ming is a Chinese dynasty famous for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Serving tea from the best porcelain teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: Pouring looks like serving tea, but it is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming with rain means raining very heavily, the same as rain pouring down.

clue.text: Return of Wagner's The Ring in repeat performance

indicators.note: return means going back, so the German article is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: Der is German for the, as in Der Ring des Nibelungen
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle is being staged again.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera cycle is Der Ring des Nibelungen, so his 'The' is German.
explanation.definitionFit: A redo is a second attempt at doing something, like giving a show again.

clue.text: Getting ready

blocks.note: surface reading: preparing to go; setter's reading: obtaining ready money, the slang word for banknotes
ready, or the readies, is British slang for available money

explanation.walkthrough: Ready is a noun here: the ready or readies is British slang for money on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning a cheque or bond into notes and coins is the act of obtaining money in hand.
